A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Speech-to-LaTeX work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original model evaluations on S2L-equations, S2L-sentences and MathSpeech, including CER and TeXBLEU results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results and adds an analysis of prediction errors in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: The ASR post-correction and direct audio-LLM approaches retain their model families, objectives and procedures. Newly disclosed LoRA settings do not establish a change to the implemented methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use English and Russian isolated equations, English mathematical sentences, and the MathSpeech benchmark. Dataset sources and human/synthetic speech coverage are retained; no new task or test environment is evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MathSpeech, Qwen variants, SALMONN, Gemma, Audio Flamingo, and the additional appendix models. TeXpert is newly cited but is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 adds exact-match and character-overlap diagnostics, including an overlap threshold of 0.8. Existing benchmark splits, CER/TeXBLEU evaluation and training budgets remain unchanged; newly supplied split sizes and LoRA details document existing experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.5 examines whether prediction errors are local or structural, with examples of symbol substitutions, index errors, text–math boundaries and fractions. Existing tokenizer, case-sensitivity, multilingual and synthetic-data analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new error counts describe predictions rather than uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark scores remain identical, including v1 Tables 4, 6 and 7 versus v2 Tables 2, 4 and 5, and Appendix Tables 10–16. V2 adds approximately 1.8k exact-match failures among 2.8k equations, with over half of the mismatches exceeding 0.8 character overlap, and an equation-length statistic of 84% between 3 and 50 symbols.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the same metric definitions and formulas. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed MathSpeech advantage from more than 40 to more than 36 percentage points, consistent with its retained 27% versus 64% comparison. Dataset novelty and the principal contribution claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 newly interprets errors as predominantly local lexical, index and text–math boundary discrepancies, with structural failures uncommon. Appendix C.1 adds a practical argument for smaller post-correction models in resource-constrained settings; the main limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, the TagMe annotation platform, split sizes and annotation proportions, LoRA configurations, and clarification that few-shot models were not fine-tuned. However, Appendix B removes v1's explicit few-shot system prompt and five examples.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Kale and Nadadur's TeXpert benchmark and its reference. The broader related-work coverage and positioning relative to MathSpeech remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the principal section sequence are retained. V2 shortens the results discussion, expands and renames Appendix A.1, adds an error-analysis subsection, an LLM usage statement and acknowledgments, and updates affiliations and cross-references.

P2.justification: The two-column main text and references are converted to a single-column ICLR layout, substantially changing typography, spacing, and figure/table sizing and placement. V1 Tables 1–2 move to Appendix A.1 as v2 Tables 6–7. Both figures and all sixteen tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves transparency through split statistics, implementation details and code-access information, corrects the abstract's numerical margin, and adds useful error analysis. Removing the explicit few-shot prompt and examples weakens self-contained reproducibility, but the added clarifications support a limited net improvement. The main methods and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
